title: Target costing: price first, cost last
caption_hook: Why do companies fix the price before the product even exists?

lines.say: Wait... companies fix the price before they even make the phone?
Yes! That's target costing. The market sets the price, not the company.
Hmm, then how does the company make any profit?
Say customers will pay ₹10,000 for a phone. Not a rupee more.
The company wants ₹2,000 profit. So the phone must cost at most ₹8,000.
Oh! So ₹8,000 is the target cost!
Exactly! Target cost equals target selling price, minus target profit.

board.title: THE FORMULA
board.sub: TSP: target price · TP: target profit

lines.say: So normally it's cost plus profit... and here it's the other way round?
Right! Here, price minus profit gives the cost you can afford.
But what if the engineers say it'll cost ₹9,000?
Then that extra ₹1,000 is the cost gap. They close it with value engineering.
Oh, like same features, but a smarter design and a lower cost!
